newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - April 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - April 25.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Friday:
WASHINGTON - Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott endorsed a global treaty banning chemical weapons and predicted its approval as treaty supporters easily won preliminary test votes.

WASHINGTON - In the campaign to win Senate approval of the treaty banning chemical weapons, the Clinton administration gave Senate Republicans concessions on a range of other national security issues.

WASHINGTON - The FBI has obtained substantial evidence that "top" Chinese officials approved plans in 1995 to attempt to buy influence with American politicians and that scheme continued through the 1996 election and is ongoing.
WASHINGTON - Montgomery County school officials contacted authorities at least 12 times to express concern for the safety of a child found bruised and emaciated in his family's apartment this week.
WASHINGTON - D.C. police and firefighters shut down a three-block area after a leaking package in the B'nai B'rith mail room sparked a chemical hazard alert.

DENVER - Repeatedly assailing Timothy McVeigh as "twisted" a federal prosecutor portrayed the accused Oklahoma City bomber as a calculating terrorist whose warped sense of patriotism drove him to kill 168 people in hopes of starting a popular uprising against the federal government.
